_comment: Three quality tiers of the same goods. Premium runs roughly 1.5x Valley, which is
realistic for most produce and dairy.
Truffle is deliberately the exception: 1.80 / 2.60 / 6.50 is a far wider spread than
anything else here. Real truffle prices genuinely swing that hard by season and grade,
and it makes sourcing a single ingredient capable of destroying a single dish - which
is a much more interesting decision than every ingredient moving together.

suppliers.name: Atlantic National Foodservice
_comment: THE DECISION EXPANSION UNLOCKS, and the one that cannot exist at a single restaurant.
About 18% under Valley per unit and a grade below it, which on its own would just be
a cheaper option anyone would take. What makes it a trade is daysInTransit: bulk
ships through a depot, so a four-day fish lands with one day left while the store
cupboard is untouched. Measured over 180 days at four sites: a card built on things
that keep earns 256,562 against 238,930 local, and a card built on fish collapses.
minimumWeeklyVolume was set to 3000 first and NOBODY could ever reach it -- six
restaurants shift about 1,600 a week. Measured rather than guessed: one site does
~250, so 1000 opens the account at four sites, which is the intended moment.
